invariants.statement: Every strength row passes exactly one phase step: sets = min(row cap, phase dose of the count the exercise would otherwise have that day); reps in reserve = max(row floor, phase minimum). Race week and post-event: main lifts only, raceWeekStrengthSets / postEventStrengthSets sets, at least raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir in reserve; specific and taper: at least 3 in reserve
No generated or proposed strength row is above its day's phase dose, whatever produced it (final validation); a session never moves into a day with another phase

After any performed re-establishment, whatever the state's mode, the count rises at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, from the re-establishment count before its phase reduction, up to the count the exercise would otherwise have

A review reads what each row prescribed (its exposure) and what was executed: the first executed exposure decides the week's kind, the last executed one its counts; rows written before R7-A are classified with the rules that wrote them
An exercise not in use this week does not change the dose of the exercises in use (return-entry week)
Unknown is never given a value: a set without reps is neither met nor missed; a record without a complete dose never displaces one with it
The same canonical facts under another source label give the same decision
An exact replay or an agreeing second report changes no decision; contradictory reports of one session are a conflict in any arrival order
A load reported in a convention other than the planned one is unknown and asked, never relabelled or adopted
The carried record is append-only: normalizing it again keeps every correction live and every superseded fact inert
A fact stated for dates is never applied beyond them
A race's duration is its event window: a finished race is complete

r7aFindings.statement: Under STRENGTH and MAINTAIN goals an accessory's rep target depends on its load mode: establishment and from-log rows use goal reps + 2 (up to 15), known rows clamp to the goal's rep range, so reps fall 7 -> 6 (STRENGTH) or 10 -> 8 (MAINTAIN) when the load becomes known. Neither rule is declared in the policy
r7aFindings.reason: Choosing the accessory rep target is a sporting decision for the SSCTR in the strength-programming work of R7-B; R7-A does not invent it

r6Items.reason: C01: fixed on R7A-FREEZE-1 (SSCTR R7A-SSCTR-r1 RESOLVED); the second cycle opened the equivalent path D56 (SSCTR R7A-SSCTR-r2), so under §16 it is not closed on R7A-FREEZE-2

C02. SSCTR R7A-SSCTR-r1: D54 RESOLVED; on R7A-FREEZE-2 the SSCTR phase grid equals FREEZE-1 and the engineering re-check (R7A-QE-r2) found no row above its day phase. The R7-A runtime as a whole is not accepted (closure.blockers)

R7-A reclassifies no earlier result; the R5 corpus replays identically (24/24) through the R7-A runtime
R7-A outputs live in CoachingCore/r7 (regression, probes); R6 official outputs stay FREEZE-1 history

Structured intake design (asking pregnancy/postpartum status again); with Product/Data and the SSCTR
Clinical-screen lexicon false positives at returns and reviews; with the SSCTR before use beyond the offline reference
Tied to G03 (sessions inside a declared pause)
